Objective neurocognitive impairment before adjuvant treatment is associated with roughly twice the hazard of death in adult diffuse glioma, an association that persisted in most adjusted analyses and was clearest in high-grade disease. Adjustment sets were incomplete and risk of bias was often high, so independence from established prognostic factors needs confirmation in individual-participant analyses. Brief standardised testing should be evaluated in prognostic models and trial stratification.

paper_title: Pavement Characteristics and Energy Pathways in Battery-Electric Road Vehicles: A Critical Review of Measurement Boundaries and Validation Gaps
paper_abstract: This focused critical review examines how pavement roughness, surface texture, and road classification relate to reported energy outcomes in battery-electric road vehicles. The evidence set comprises 55 publications—including original investigations, methodological comparators, reviews, conference proceedings, and datasets—purposively assembled from existing project records rather than selected through formal systematic screening. Studies are compared by pavement exposure, vehicle type, energy-accounting boundary, measured or simulated outcome, and validation target. Skar et al. report a 3.4% increase in normalized energy for each 1 m/km increase in the International Roughness Index (IRI), but this outcome is not directly measured battery-terminal electricity. Jonas et al. calculate energy from measured battery current and voltage across functional road classes without isolating pavement roughness. Beckers et al. estimate tire and suspension energy dissipation using a model validated for suspension motion on a diesel bus and subsequently applied to a battery-electric bus. Wang et al. (2023) and Singh et al. (2025) model losses associated with road irregularities rather than directly measure roughness-related battery-pack energy demand. The 704% figure reported by Singh et al. concerns modeled mechanical dissipation; the corresponding electricity estimates depend on an assumed drivetrain efficiency. Two related publications from 2025–2026 share tire finite-element model specifications, raising questions about study independence. Earlier pavement–electric-vehicle reviews also limit claims of originality. Differences in pavement exposure, energy-accounting boundaries, and validation prevent the derivation of a defensible pooled roughness-to-battery-energy coefficient from this evidence set. This article is a focused critical review, not a completed PRISMA systematic review.

paper_title: A Survey on Image Restoration in the Foundation Model Era
paper_abstract: Foundation models provide transferable representations, generative priors, and multimodal understanding, offering new ways to address diverse image degradations and restoration requirements. This survey reviews three complementary directions: leveraging existing foundation models for image restoration, developing restoration-oriented foundation models, and coordinating restoration models and tools through agents. We examine how pretrained representations, generative priors, and additional supervision support image restoration. For restoration-oriented foundation models, we compare pretraining, unified modeling, and adaptation strategies across tasks and domains. For agentic image restoration, we examine how agents coordinate restoration models and tools within a unified framework for diverse tasks through task planning, tool selection, feedback-driven refinement, and experience retrieval. We summarize reported benchmark results and model budgets to examine the strengths and limitations of existing methods, taking into account differences in training coverage, adaptation, and evaluation settings. Finally, we discuss challenges and future directions in generalization and adaptation to real-world degradations, faithful and user-controllable restoration, reliable assessment for agents, and efficient and reproducible deployment. A curated list of works reviewed in this survey is available at https://github.com/mrluin/Awesome-IR-in-FM-era.

paper_title: Structured Medication Review and Deprescribing Across Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review of Implementation Drivers and AI-Driven Horizons
paper_abstract: Background: Population ageing, prevalence of multimorbidity, polypharmacy and frailty considerably increase the complexity of pharmacological treatment in older adults and the risk of medication-related harm. Medication review (MR) represents a key strategy to assess treatment appropriateness, support medication optimization and identify opportunities for deprescribing. However, its implementation in routine clinical practice remains heterogeneous and inconsistent. Methods: A narrative review was conducted focusing on MR conceptual framework, assessment and deprescribing tools, interprofessional collaboration, implementation strategies, and emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-supported technologies across different healthcare settings. Relevant literature was identified through searches on PubMed, Google Scholar and Scopus, complemented by reference-list screening and citation tracking. Recent literature was prioritized, while seminal publications and guidelines were retained when relevant to the development of key concepts. Results: MR encompasses different approaches, ranging from structured medication assessment to comprehensive holistic processes incorporating clinical judgement and shared decision-making. Explicit and implicit tools can support the identification of potentially inappropriate medications and other drug-related problems, while deprescribing approaches facilitate the reassessment and discontinuation of unnecessary medications. Evidence also highlights the importance of pharmacists and interprofessional collaboration, patient involvement, workflow integration, and organizational support for successful implementation. Digital and AI-based approaches, including electronic health record-integrated clinical decision support systems, may further support medication optimization. Conclusions: MR should be considered a dynamic and collaborative process rather than a one-time assessment of medication lists. Future efforts should focus on its sustainable integration into routine care, continuity across healthcare settings, standardized implementation strategies, and the validation of digital tools that complement clinical judgement.

paper_title: Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality in Thoracic Surgery: Current Applications and Objective Assessment of Surgical Competency—A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) are increasingly utilized across the perioperative continuum in thoracic surgery. We performed a systematic review to elucidate the clinical utility of AR/VR technologies in general thoracic surgery, identify current technological trends, and evaluate their role as objective assessment tools for surgical competency. Methods: A comprehensive systematic search of the PubMed database was conducted from inception through 6 June 2026 in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eligible peer-reviewed studies were categorized according to their clinical phase of utilization, perioperative surgical outcomes, and objective simulator-derived competency metrics. Results: A total of 1,013 records were initially identified, of which 74 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed. Clinical applications of AR/VR in thoracic surgery spanned three principal domains: (1) surgical education and training, (2) preoperative anatomical planning and resection simulation, and (3) real-time intraoperative navigation (encompassing non-anatomical tumor localization and anatomical bronchovascular guidance). Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) further accelerated three-dimensional anatomical segmentation and intraoperative registration workflows. Across nine comparative cohort studies, AR/VR or three-dimensional guidance was associated with significantly shorter operative times in 77.8% (7/9) and lower estimated intraoperative blood loss in 55.6% (5/9) of studies without increasing postoperative complications. Furthermore, validated VR simulation platforms reliably stratified novice, intermediate, and experienced surgeons using automated kinematic metrics. Conclusions: AR and VR technologies enhance surgical training, complex segmentectomy planning, and intraoperative navigation. Standardized VR scoring systems incorporating procedural time, simulated blood loss, and instrument motion dynamics are warranted to advance objective surgical credentialing.

paper_title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
paper_abstract: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only above the level of the single judgment. We ground each claim in a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system (541621 reviewer events, 483 reviewers), and find that a purely behavioral expertise profile inverts the ground truth, scoring an overconfident cohort (5.2 percent correction survival) higher than genuine experts (99.2 percent); that reviewer quality is flat across tenure, so the trait is not learned on the job; and that the same calibration logic that separates good from bad reviewers, applied to the model, concentrates 92.5 percent of human effort on genuine errors. We close with the boundary the theory must respect: under majority-vote aggregation, individual causal value is unidentifiable.
comments: Accepted at the Thirteenth Annual Conference on Advances in Cognitive Systems (ACS), Edinburgh, United Kingdom, October 6-9, 2026. Awarded one of 2026 Ada Lovelace Awardees for Excellent Paper Submissions to ACS

paper_title: Urban State Representation for Autonomous Mobility: A Survey of Multimodal Perception, Architectures, Datasets, and Benchmarks
paper_abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead, and the GNSS traces of millions of trips. Yet most learned representations are built for one platform, one city, and one task. We survey this fragmented landscape through a single lens, the Urban State Representation (USR): a georeferenced, layered, time-varying, uncertainty-aware state that any sensing platform can write to and any downstream task can read from. We (i) formalize USR and five desiderata for it, and relate it to bird's-eye-view (BEV) features, occupancy, vectorized maps, neural fields and 3D Gaussians, scene graphs, road-network graphs, language tokens, and world-model latents; (ii) organize sensing platforms, cross-view (ground-aerial) matching, fusion operators, 3D geometric foundation models, end-to-end and vision-language-action models, and generative world models and data engines in one taxonomy that spans sensors to decisions; (iii) compile 26 urban datasets and simulators across ego, cooperative (V2X), aerial, trajectory, and language settings, with a metric glossary, a cross-benchmark results snapshot, a trend analysis, and a platform-coverage gap analysis; and (iv) review applications and propose, as an outlook, USR-5, a five-test protocol with explicit references and one aggregate score for measuring whether a state is shared, together with a research agenda of six open problems covering cross-city and cross-sensor transfer, uncertainty, efficiency, sim-to-real evaluation, and governance. This survey is an entry point for computer vision, autonomous driving, transportation, and urban computing researchers; the paper list, datasets, and USR-5 code are at https://github.com/binayksingh/Awesome-Urban-State-Representation.
comments: Accepted to the UrbanState Workshop at WACV 2027. 8 pages + references + 5-page supplementary appendix. Code and data: https://github.com/binayksingh/Awesome-Urban-State-Representation

paper_title: Where the Cost of Endometriosis Falls: Diagnostic Delay, Treatment and Productivity Loss—A Review with a Europe-Wide Burden Estimate
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Endometriosis affects about one in ten women of reproductive age, yet its economic consequences are documented almost entirely at the individual patient level. We reviewed the evidence on diagnostic workup, treatment and work absenteeism, and used those inputs to build the aggregate estimate Europe lacks. Methods: Eight pre-specified PubMed/MEDLINE queries, citation chasing and five foundational studies yielded 69 reports; screening followed PRISMA 2020, each study was appraised with the instrument matched to its design, and all costs harmonised to 2024 international dollars (Int$). Those inputs fed a prevalence-based cost-of-illness model over 31 countries, reported to CHEERS 2022. Results: Across the reviewed evidence diagnostic delay behaves as a cost multiplier rather than a marker of severity, and indirect costs equal or exceed direct costs wherever burden is decomposed. Harmonisation is itself a finding: on a common price basis the published estimates rise unequally, and most in the lower-price systems most likely to borrow foreign figures. One patient-year costs Int$18,948. Across 112.4 million women aged 15–49, the prevalence recorded in payer claims — Hungary supplies the only European figure — implies Int$1.3 billion a year; an assumed population prevalence of ten per cent implies Int$213.0 billion, 0.62 per cent of pooled purchasing-power-adjusted gross domestic product, 1.17 million quality-adjusted life years and 2.92 million lifetime working-life years. The 159-fold distance between the two combines a 50.8-fold difference in who is counted with a 3.1-fold difference in which costs are admitted; prevalence dominates its uncertainty. Conclusions: Whether earlier diagnosis repays its cost is not tested: the model evaluates no intervention.

paper_title: Before Peer Review: Partnership Networks and Access to Canadian Health Research Funding
paper_abstract: Funding competitions that require an implementing partner make access to research partly dependent on relationships established before peer review. Using a Canadian Institutes of Health Research youth mental health competition, this commentary examines that barrier for newcomers to partnership networks, with particular attention to Black researchers and Black-led organizations. Canada has relevant planning mechanisms, including support from the Institute of Neurosciences, Mental Health and Addiction. The proposed adaptation is to align exploratory funding with competition deadlines, allow initial expressions of interest before formal partnership commitments, and fund community and youth participation in planning. Funders should monitor progression from registration to submission and seek brief, voluntary feedback on partnership formation. Such monitoring should protect privacy, acknowledge incomplete coverage and nonresponse, and respect organizations’ freedom to decline collaboration.

paper_title: Operational Analytics and Artificial Intelligence for Maritime Decarbonization: A Reference-Based Review and Five-Stage Decision-Support Framework
paper_abstract: Background. International shipping has to deliver near-term greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions while the industry moves toward fuels and propulsion systems with much lower life-cycle emissions. Until those fuels are available at scale, the way ships are navigated, monitored and maintained is the lever operators can pull today.Scope. This narrative review draws together published maritime policy, peer-reviewed research and identifiable industry studies, and uses them to develop a five-stage framework for data-driven operational efficiency: (1) data acquisition, (2) quality control and integration, (3) visualization and monitoring, (4) predictive modeling and (5) decision support with feedback. It is not an empirical performance study. This review did not train new fuel-consumption models or measure fleet-wide savings, and every number reported here is attributed to its original source and kept in its original context.Findings. In a retrospective, simulation-based study of bulk-carrier voyages, NAPA, ClassNK and Marubeni reported potential fuel and CO₂ reductions of up to 7.3% from voyage optimization and an average Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) improvement of 5–6% [7]. DNV estimated that combined operational and technical efficiency measures could cut global-fleet fuel consumption by 4–16% by 2030 [8]. A peer-reviewed data-fusion study of eight containerships reported test-set R² values of 0.74–0.90 for selected machine-learning models [9]. These figures describe different vessels, methods and outcomes, and they cannot be added together to produce a universal benefit of integration.Contribution. The paper offers a source-grounded systems architecture, a scheme for attributing evidence to what it can and cannot support, and a prospective evaluation protocol for testing whether integrated analytics improves operational performance beyond isolated interventions.

paper_title: Recovery, Quantification, and Stabilization of 2-Acetyl-1-Pyrroline from Pandanus amaryllifolius: A Critical Review of Extraction Technologies and Industrial Translation
paper_abstract: 2-Acetyl-1-pyrroline (2AP) is a highly odor-active compound responsible for much of the characteristic pandan-like and popcorn-like aroma of Pandanus amaryllifolius leaves and aromatic rice. Recovering a commercially useful natural aroma requires more than maximizing crude botanical extract mass: raw-material selection, extraction selectivity, analytical comparability, downstream losses, stability, and sensory delivery must be addressed together. This critical narrative review evaluates foundational solvent and supercritical carbon dioxide extraction studies, the 2022 response-surface optimization of ultrasound-assisted ethanol extraction, and relevant evidence through November 2026 on drying, leaf maturity, aroma profiling, and encapsulation. In the 2022 study, an experimentally validated condition of 20 min, 60% ethanol, 25% nominal sonicator amplitude, and 12.5 g leaves in 200 mL solvent yielded 60.51% crude extract and 1.43 ppm reported 2AP. However, its experimental design also included a run reporting 4.873 ppm 2AP, showing that the reported optimum should not be interpreted as the highest measured 2AP concentration. Moreover, published results express 2AP in non-equivalent units and use differing raw-material pretreatments and analytical platforms. Subsequent studies demonstrate that freeze-drying can better conserve 2AP than hot-air drying, that leaf position influences 2AP concentration, and that aroma perception depends on multiple odorants. Encapsulation work suggests strategies to reduce 2AP loss, but its performance cannot be generalized to every food formulation. We propose a process-development framework based on validated 2AP recovery per mass of dry leaf, odor activity, solvent acceptability, retention after concentration and drying, shelf-life stability, and process economics. The evidence supports ultrasound-assisted extraction as a promising option, not as a universally superior technology; matched analytical and pilot-scale comparisons remain necessary.

paper_title: Customer Feedback Analysis with a Business Taxonomy and Budgeted Review Selection: An Offline Evaluation
paper_abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises need feedback analyses that identify actionable issues under limited review budgets. We link a declared business taxonomy, multi-label classification, budgeted review queues, and convention-weighted issue priorities. SemEval-2016 laptop annotations are mapped deterministically to seven analytical labels, and no new human labels are claimed. On 808 held-out laptop fragments, lexicon-augmented logistic regression reaches macro F1 0.4778 against 0.4572 for plain logistic regression, yet the plain model has fewer joint state errors (672 versus 687) and lower priority mean absolute error (MAE: 0.01344 versus 0.01768). At a 10% budget the validated joint queue finds 109 of 687 state errors against 100 for uncertainty and 68.56 for random selection. Perfect replacement of selected fragments lowers error counts but raises priority MAE for the impact-only queue, because contributions are signed. Claims are limited to the 808 held-out fragments: offline queue discovery compares predictions with supplied gold states, ideal correction assumes perfect replacement, and neither measures observed reviewer effectiveness.

paper_title: Body Composition Monitoring in Older Adults on GLP-1 Receptor Agonists A Narrative Review of Assessment Methods
paper_abstract: Objective: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) produce marked weight loss. A meaningful proportion of that loss is lean tissue including muscle, and the effects of GLP-1RAs on bone remain uncertain. Older adults are vulnerable to morbidity and mortality caused by muscle and bone density loss, and body weight alone cannot detect these changes. This narrative literature review evaluated body composition assessment methods for monitoring older adults receiving GLP-1RAs. Methods: PubMed was searched from inception to August 2026. Studies were included if they evaluated the accuracy, repeatability, or ability to detect change of a body composition assessment method in adults. Methods were grouped as reference-standard, clinically accessible, or emerging scalable technologies. Results: Thirteen studies were included (nine primary studies and four reviews or methodological guides). Two primary studies enrolled older adults, and one measured body composition during GLP-1RA treatment. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) was the most practical reference method because it assesses lean mass, fat mass, and bone mineral density in one scan, but its precision declined with obesity and estimates differed between systems. Bioelectrical impedance analysis was highly repeatable, but accuracy varied widely between devices. Smartphone applications and three-dimensional optical imaging were the most scalable, but their apparent accuracy depended on the reference system and participant posture, and neither has been validated in older adults or for tracking change. None of the accessible or emerging methods measured bone. Conclusions: No current method is both valid and scalable for monitoring body composition in older adults receiving GLP-1RAs. Longitudinal validation in this population, with agreement reported on change scores, is needed before monitoring-guided care can be tested.

paper_title: A Review of the Gut Microbiota as a Regulator of Muscle Quality and Flavor in Farmed Fish
paper_abstract: As aquaculture shifts focus from yield to edible product attributes, muscle quality (encompassing texture, nutritional composition, and oxidative stability) alongside ﬂavor proﬁles collectively determine consumer acceptance and economic value. Emerging evidence indicates that the gut microbiota, operating through the microbiota–gut–muscle axis, can regulate nutrient absorption, lipid and amino acid metabolism, extracellular matrix deposition, and the synthesis of ﬂavor-active metabolites. This review synthesizes research spanning the two decades from the ﬁrst gnotobiotic zebraﬁsh experiments to the present, integrating gnotobiotic models, 16S rRNA surveys, metagenomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, alongside dietary interventions in commercially important species. The conceptual trajectory is traced from early host-microbiota interdependence in zebraﬁsh to recent causal demonstrations that speciﬁc bacteria and their metabolites alter muscle collagen synthesis and ﬂesh ﬂavor. Evidence linking microbiota composition to muscle texture, taste-active compounds, volatile aromas, and geosmin/2-methylisoborneol related oﬀ-ﬂavors is critically evaluated, while modulation strategies including probiotics, prebiotics, and RAS management are assessed. Finally, critical knowledge gaps, notably the scarcity of causal evidence and neglect of host sex and genetics, are identiﬁed, and precision modulation framework is proposed. This framework matches microbiome-informed interventions to speciﬁc species, life stages, and production systems and is designed to guide interventions aimed at improving ﬁsh muscle quality and ﬂavor, with eﬀectiveness to be validated experimentally.

paper_title: Synthetic Data Generation in the Era of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
paper_abstract: Background: The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has dramatically advanced the capabilities of Natural Language Processing (NLP), enabling breakthroughs in text understanding, generation, and reasoning. However, the success of these models hinges on access to massive, diverse, and high-quality labeled datasets. In many real-world scenarios, such as specialized domains (e.g., healthcare, law), low-resource languages, and privacy-sensitive applications, curating such data remains prohibitively expensive, time-consuming, or infeasible due to regulatory or ethical constraints. Moreover, as LLMs continue to scale in size and complexity, the demand for training and evaluation data grows disproportionately, exacerbating annotation bottlenecks and domain coverage gaps. Synthetic Data Generation (SDG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm to address these challenges by programmatically producing task-specific or domain-adapted examples that complement or replace manually labeled data. Initially grounded in statistical modeling and deep generative architectures, SDG has evolved into a central strategy for improving data efficiency, mitigating distributional shifts, and enabling scalable supervision in modern NLP pipelines, especially in conjunction with LLM-driven prompt-based learning and self-supervised generation. Objectives: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of SDG techniques up to November 2026, with a particular focus on LLM-oriented pipelines. We categorize generative approaches for synthetic text, identify trends in controllability, verification and automation, and highlight open challenges in evaluation, fairness, privacy and scalability. Methods: We review the model families used to generate synthetic text, including probabilistic models, autoencoders and variational autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), transformers, diffusion language models and mixtures of experts, as background for LLM-based pipelines such as instruction synthesis, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt evolution, feedback loops and multi-agent generation, together with toolkits such as PromptSource [1], Self-Instruct [2] and LM-Debugger [3]. The original literature was collected informally; we extended it with a documented search run on 14 November 2026 (49 queries, 78 candidate records, 47 works added) covering 2025–2026 work on reasoning traces and verifiable rewards, model collapse and data quality, agentic and multi-agent pipelines, and evaluation, privacy and multilingual generation. The scope is text and language data, with other data types only where an LLM generates or directs their generation, and every reference was checked against arXiv, Crossref or the publisher. Results: Our synthesis traces an evolution from static, single-model pipelines to modular, verifier-centred and agentic systems in which LLMs plan, generate, critique and check data. Since 2025, synthetic data has become central to teaching models to reason: verifiable rewards move the bottleneck from preference labels to problems with checkable answers, which procedural generators, rephrased web text and self-play now supply. Studies of model collapse show that accumulating real and synthetic data avoids collapse while replacing real data does not, but also that even small synthetic fractions and recursive training can degrade models and their fairness. Synthetic text can leak membership information about its source data, and differentially private generation methods are narrowing the utility gap. Evaluation practice remains fragmented, and multilingual generation increasingly relies on culturally grounded rather than translated data. Conclusions: LLM-driven SDG is rapidly transforming data creation, making it more scalable, controllable and adaptive, but its reliability now depends on verification, provenance and privacy safeguards. This survey offers a taxonomy and a roadmap for building trustworthy synthetic data systems, and it motivates future work on verifiers beyond checkable domains, standardized evaluation of data generators, collapse-aware data practice and formal privacy guarantees.

paper_title: Radiological Manifestations of Invasive Fungal Infections in Emergency Settings: A Comprehensive Review
paper_abstract: Invasive fungal infections can present with rapidly progressive tissue injury before microbiological confirmation is available. Emergency imaging must identify the affected organ, detect complications and guide further diagnostic assessment. This narrative review synthesizes selected imaging studies and consensus guidance on computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography in adult emergency and acute-care settings. Findings are interpreted according to fungal biology, host immune status and disease timing. Pulmonary manifestations include angioinvasive and airway-predominant patterns; sinonasal assessment emphasizes extrasinus extension, tissue viability and orbital or intracranial complications. Central nervous system imaging addresses abscesses, infarction and haemorrhage, while abdominal and urinary assessment identifies visceral lesions, bowel compromise and obstruction. Critical appraisal of selected studies highlights limitations related to patient selection, small samples, reference standards and transferability of diagnostic estimates. The review connects these findings to examination selection, vascular assessment, urgent communication and sampling targets through a proposed clinical workflow. Imaging supports suspicion and defines disease extent but cannot independently establish fungal aetiology. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether integrated imaging pathways improve diagnostic timing and patient outcomes.

paper_title: Beyond the Model: A Survey of Harness Software for Embodied Agents
paper_abstract: Embodied foundation models produce impressive demonstrations, but executing long, complex tasks depends on software outside the model, just as in the ransition from ChatGPT to Codex. We call that software the embodied agent harness and divide it into planning, skill acquisition, memory, monitoring, and self-evolution. The papers come from robotics, machine learning, and embodied-AI venues, 2022--2026. About a fifth of the citations are preprints or non-archival manuscripts, mostly for new directions. Open problems remain in efficiency, robustness, generalizability, model availability, multi-robot orchestration, and evaluation.

paper_title: Contained or Escaped? Measuring Sandbox Escape and Auto-Reviewer Decisions in AI Coding Agents
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents now run shell commands in a default sandbox and must request permission, often screened by a large language model (LLM) auto-reviewer, before a command may use the network or write outside the workspace. Most prompt-injection benchmarks for coding agents assume unrestricted execution. We built SARD-Bench, 240 poisoned-workspace cases in four families and three stealth tiers, with a harness whose single tool makes the agent declare and justify the permissions it needs. We ran Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-5.1 and Llama 4 Maverick once per case (720 trajectories), executed the two-turn family in a macOS Seatbelt sandbox, and had a GPT-4o-mini reviewer judge every harmful command with and without the agent’s rationale. All labels were audited by hand in two passes. The two proprietary models ran the payload inside the sandbox in 28.3% of runs and requested the privileges to escape in 6.5%. Llama 4 Maverick escaped in 44.6%. Stealthier files raised in-sandbox execution from 10.6% to 50.6% but left escape rates unchanged. With the agent’s rationale, the reviewer blocked 126 of 138 escape requests, against 64 from the command alone. Claude Sonnet 5.5 returned provider refusals in 140 runs, and an indicator-matching scorer missed half of all escapes. Evaluations of sandboxed agents should report where a payload would run and audit their labels by hand.

paper_title: Probiotics for Vaginal Dysbiosis and Recurrent Bacterial Vaginosis: A Narrative Review of Strain-Specific Evidence
paper_abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common manifestation of vaginal dysbiosis, and recurrence after antimicrobial therapy remains frequent. This narrative review examines the rationale for restoring vaginal lactobacilli and evaluates oral and intravaginal interventions using selected clinical trials, evidence syntheses, and practice guidance. In a phase 2b trial, intravaginal Lactobacillus crispatus CTV-05 following metronidazole reduced 12-week recurrence from 45% to 30%. Trials of oral Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GR-1 plus Limosilactobacillus reuteri RC-14 reported inconsistent short-term cure outcomes. Meta-analyses suggest a reduction in BV recurrence with some preparations, with uncertainty arising from differences in strains, formulations, timing, and outcome definitions. Small trials of vaginal prebiotic gels report improvements in microbiological measures, while evidence for durable benefit remains limited. Available data provide insufficient support for extrapolating BV findings to vulvovaginal candidiasis, human papillomavirus clearance, or shiitake-derived adjuncts. The clearest evidence concerns specific interventions tested after standard BV treatment. Future trials should measure symptomatic recurrence alongside strain persistence and assess whether protection persists after dosing ends.

paper_title: Beyond General Anxiety Screening: Anxiety Subtypes in People with Multiple Sclerosis in Argentina—A Cross-Sectional Online Survey
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Anxiety is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), but screening relies on general instruments that may miss specific presentations. We described anxiety subtypes in people with MS in Argentina, estimated how many cases a general screen would miss, and explored correlates and pre-diagnostic psychiatric symptoms. Methods: Cross-sectional online survey (March–May 2026) of adults with self-reported MS using the anxiety subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-A), GAD-7, Social Phobia Inventory, Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory-Revised, Patient Health Questionnaire panic module and Fear Questionnaire, plus questions on pre-onset symptoms. Results: Of 84 participants (76.2% women; 79.8% relapsing-remitting), 41.7% scored HADS-A ≥ 8. Social anxiety (26.2%) was the most frequent subtype, followed by generalized anxiety (21.4%), obsessive-compulsive symptoms (20.2%) and panic disorder (11.9%). Among HADS-A-negative participants, 14.3% (95% CI 7.1–26.7%) screened positive for at least one subtype. Female gender and relapsing-remitting MS were associated with higher general and generalized anxiety scores, younger age with social anxiety, and disability with agoraphobic avoidance. Overall, 71.4% reported anxiety-related symptoms before MS onset; of these, 38.3% had consulted a specialist and 20.0% had received a psychiatric diagnosis. Conclusions: Anxiety in MS is frequent and heterogeneous. General screening alone may miss subtype-specific cases, and psychiatric symptoms often precede the MS diagnosis.

paper_title: Diffusion Models for Embodied Perception and World Modeling: A Survey from a Humanoid Robotics Perspective
paper_abstract: Humanoid intelligence requires agents to perceive uncertain environments, infer structured representations from multimodal sensory observations, and predict future world evolution before acting. Otherwise, recent advances in diffusion models have extended their role far beyond image synthesis, enabling probabilistic perception, spatial scene understanding, and predictive world modeling for embodied AI. By modeling complex data distributions through conditional generation, diffusion models naturally address uncertainty, partial observability, and multimodal future prediction, making them particularly suitable for embodied perception and predictive imagination. This survey provides a comprehensive review of diffusion models for embodied perception and world modeling. We first trace the evolution of humanoid robotics and introduce the diffusion formulations underlying the surveyed methods, and then propose a unified taxonomy that organizes existing methods from probabilistic perception to predictive imagination. We comprehensively review diffusion-based approaches for human perception, embodied self-perception, and environment understanding. For world modeling, we analyze the advantages of diffusion model for observation space prediction, compact learned latent spaces, and conditioning on explicit robot actions or latent actions inferred from video. By unifying recent advances in perception and predictive world modeling, this survey highlights diffusion models as a general probabilistic framework for embodied intelligence and outlines promising directions toward more capable and reliable embodied AI systems.

paper_title: Coronary Artery Dilatation in Febrile Children Beyond Kawasaki Disease: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Coronary artery dilatation is the hallmark cardiovascular complication of Kawasaki disease (KD), but it is not exclusive to the disease. In children with prolonged fever, increased coronary artery dimensions may also be observed in non-KD conditions, including transient fever-related changes, severe infections, systemic inflammatory disorders, and vasculitic diseases. This narrative review examines coronary artery findings in febrile children beyond KD, focusing on comparative Z-score data, the interpretive limitations of current Z-score models, infectious, inflammatory, and vasculitic associations, and the contribution of serial echocardiography to clinical interpretation. Across comparative febrile cohorts, a coronary Z-score ≥2.5 appears to strongly favour KD over non-KD febrile illnesses, whereas borderline values from 2.0 to < 2.5 may occur in both KD and non-KD febrile illness and should not be interpreted in isolation. Because Z-score classification is influenced by the regression model used, the same coronary measurement may be classified differently by different calculators. Coronary abnormalities beyond KD have been reported in association with several infectious agents and systemic inflammatory or vasculitic diseases, although much of this evidence derives from case reports and small series. Clinical context, laboratory findings, microbiological plausibility, the Z-score model applied, and serial echocardiographic evolution should therefore be integrated to support timely recognition of KD when clinically coherent, while avoiding overdiagnosis based on an isolated borderline coronary finding.

paper_title: JEPA for astronomy: multi-survey spectral alignment puts stellar parameters on the leading principal axes
paper_abstract: Spectra from different surveys carry different systematics and are not calibrated against one another. Multi-survey foundation models for stellar spectra are then built by aligning embeddings of the same star observed across surveys. Most in astronomy follow the recipes established for language and vision, aligning with a contrastive loss that separates every star from the others. However, this does not ensure that the stellar physics is encoded in a form that a simple read-out can recover. Holding the cross-survey architecture fixed and varying only the alignment loss, we measure what an objective encodes from the principal-component geometry of the Gaia BP/RP (XP) spectra and from a linear probe of the stellar parameters. In a properly aligned embedding, the leading two principal components form a plane that recovers an analog of the Kiel diagram, the third component tracks [Fe/H], and [alpha/Fe] varies coherently across the plane, such that the chemically defined Galactic disks and accreted populations occupy distinct loci. We show that legibility, the ease of reading the information out, is highest for a training objective that never pushes stars apart, and instead constrains only the overall distribution of each survey's embeddings (JEPA). JEPA also exceeds the contrastive alternative at the same architecture, and the performance improves further as more surveys (Gaia XP+LAMOST LRS+DESI+APOGEE) are included. Predicted abundances for 8.0 million XP giants reproduce the main [alpha/Fe]-[Fe/H] structure of the Milky Way. These results indicate that the choice of alignment objective, not alignment alone, determines whether stellar labels are linearly recoverable.
comments: 15 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AAS journals. Comments welcome

paper_title: A Survey on the Use of Machine Learning within Computer Algebra
paper_abstract: This survey explores the use of Machine Learning (ML) in the field of Computer Algebra (CA), both to optimise existing CA algorithms, and to perform symbolic computation directly. Traditional symbolic methods, while mathematically rigorous, often are computationally expensive thus limiting their use in real-world applications. Recent advances have shown that data-driven techniques can address these limitations by guiding heuristic decisions, selecting optimal algorithms, predicting structural properties of algebraic objects, or even making direct symbolic computations.   We take a systematic literature review approach and uncover work in CA applications including cylindrical algebraic decomposition, Gröbner basis computation, symbolic integration, and many more. The survey compares the different ML approaches that have been employed for these tasks, ranging from decision trees to transformers. Issues uncovered by the survey include the lack of benchmark datasets for CA, which hinders the comparison of methods and the generalizability of ML models. The survey identifies the potential for explainable AI tools to help develop trust in decisions, and to drive forward CA research itself.

paper_title: Digital Twins for Battery-Powered and Electric Rail Vehicles: Architectures, Prognostics, Validation and Research Priorities—A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Battery-powered and electric rail vehicles are an emerging route to decarbonising lines where overhead electrification is uneconomic, and they move a large share of vehicle dependability onto the battery system, its thermal management and power-electronic interfaces. Digital twins (DTs) virtual representations continuously calibrated to a physical asset are widely proposed to manage such systems, yet railway-specific evidence remains thin. This narrative critical review consolidates the foundations needed to design a DT for a battery-powered rail vehicle: energy-supply architectures and railway duty characteristics, lithium-ion ageing and failure mechanisms, battery model families, data infrastructure and edge–cloud partitioning, prognostics and health management, and verification, validation and standards. A four-layer reference architecture that keeps safety-related protection on the vehicle while using the cloud for calibration and fleet analytics is proposed. The review finds that the enabling methods are mature in road-vehicle and laboratory contexts but that railway-specific validation, uncertainty-aware decision support, twin qualification criteria and demonstrated operational benefit are lacking in the literature examined. A prioritised research agenda is presented. The review is narrative rather than systematic; gaps are stated relative to the sources examined.

paper_title: Experimental Evidence for Effects of Chronic Infra-Sound Exposure on the Heart – A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: This narrative review outlines potential pathophysiological mechanisms in the mammalian heart in response to chronic infrasound exposure from technical installations. Recent research findings suggest that repeated exposure to infrasound can activate the heart's mechanosensitive PIEZO-1 channels. PIEZO-1 plays an important role in cardiac contractility via modulation of Ca²⁺ release and is involved in ROS homeostasis. The increasingly widespread sources of technical infrasound - which often exhibit high sound pressure intensities at infrasonic frequencies - should be reevaluated with regard to their impact on living organisms. Experimental overexpression of cardiac PIEZO-1 in mice serves as an example of potential effects of chronic infrasound exposure on the heart. Associated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation reveals links to inflammatory pathways. Continued PIEZO-1 (over)stimulation appears to disrupt Ca²⁺ and ROS homeostasis in the long term, ultimately resulting in cardiomyopathy and arrhythmogenicity.

paper_title: Dimensional Assessment of Personality Pathology and Treatment Adaptation in Alcohol Use Disorder: From an Empty Systematic Review to a Narrative Synthesis
paper_abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) and personality disorders (PD) co-occur in up to two thirds of treatment-seeking patients, and comorbidity predicts poorer engagement and relapse. Current diagnostic frameworks (DSM-5 Alternative Model, ICD-11, HiTOP) describe personality pathology dimensionally, which is expected to be less stigmatizing, more acceptable to patients and more useful for treatment planning. We aimed to identify programs that assess personality dimensionally in patients with AUD and adapt treatment to the profile obtained. Following a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420260656442), PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (February–March 2025). Of 2,529 records, 72 were assessed in full text; none met the pre-specified criteria, so the review was converted into a narrative synthesis of the 44 closest reports plus one case report identified outside the search. Reports fell into three groups: dimensional assessment without consequences for treatment; treatment adapted to a categorical PD diagnosis (schema, psychodynamic or mentalization-based therapies) or transdiagnostic treatments that did not assess personality; and contextual evidence on comorbidity, typologies and assessment. The only near-miss relied on a categorical Millon inventory. We discuss why assessment and intervention remain disconnected and propose brief dimensional screening at treatment entry as a pathway to person-centered, less stigmatizing AUD care.

paper_title: Bambara Groundnut and Finger Millet for Instant Complementary Foods: A Narrative Critical Review of Molecular Composition, Processing-Induced Chemical Changes, Functionality and Sensory Quality
paper_abstract: Bambara groundnut (Vigna subterranea) and finger millet (Eleusine coracana) are underutilised African crops whose combination could improve the protein quality and micronutrient density of cereal-based instant complementary foods. This review examines the molecular constituents that determine their nutritional and technological value, as well as the chemical changes induced by processing. Bambara groundnut supplies lysine-rich protein and starch; nonetheless, its use is limited by phytic acid, phenolic compounds, a hard-to-cook defect linked to pectin–phytate interactions and cell wall lignification, and beany volatiles such as hexanal and 2-pentylfuran. Finger millet provides starch, calcium and phenolic acids, a large share of which are bound to cell wall polysaccharides, together with phytate and tannins that chelate minerals and bind proteins. Soaking, germination, fermentation and malting activate phytases and amylases, lowering phytate by up to 67% and finger millet paste viscosity from 1305 to 18 cP, while microwave and infrared heating gelatinise starch, aggregate proteins and shorten cooking time. Evidence for a finished product is limited to one instant porridge reported in a doctoral thesis. Future studies should link processing conditions to molecular outcomes, including phenolic and phytate profiles, starch and protein structure, volatile composition and in vitro digestibility, in a reconstituted Bambara groundnut–finger millet porridge

paper_title: NEXUSFlow: A Multi-Boat Autonomous Survey System for Locating Bank-Side Arsenic Sources in Rivers—System Design and Monte Carlo Evaluation
paper_abstract: Arsenic contamination of the Kok River in northern Thailand is currently monitored by manual sampling at fixed points, and laboratory results take three to four weeks, while the source often remains unknown. We present NEXUSFlow, a monitoring system in which a fleet of five autonomous surface vehicles surveys a river reach along automatically planned zigzag routes, a plume-mapping model (PatternTrack AI) estimates the contaminant field and traces its source, and an AI agent (NATEE) drafts a response plan that is released only after approval by a pollution control officer and a village leader. To test the central design choice—mobile zigzag sampling instead of fixed stations—we ran a Monte Carlo simulation of 2,000 bank-side discharges in a 12 km reach using a two-dimensional transverse-mixing model with reflecting banks. The median full-mixing length was 46 km, so plumes remained attached to one bank throughout the reach. In the 1,776 scenarios in which some location exceeded 0.01 mg/L, seven fixed stations on one bank detected the plume in 38% of cases, stations on both banks in 75%, mid-channel stations in 2% and a centreline boat in 4%, whereas a 40-sample zigzag survey detected 83%. A short follow-up along the affected bank reduced the median source-location error to 15 m, compared with about 830 m for fixed stations. The ranking was unchanged for strongly meandering reaches. A prototype run on simulated data took 81 min from the first report to a village alert. The results support combining mobile zigzag surveys with fixed stations and must be confirmed by field tests.

paper_title: Deep-Learning Prediction of Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatographic Retention Times for Small Molecules and Pharmaceuticals: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Predicted retention times can narrow candidate lists in liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC–HRMS). Deep-learning models report errors near the variability between repeated measurements, but their credibility depends on the evaluation design. We reviewed deep-learning retention-time prediction for non-polymeric small molecules in reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RP-LC). Searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through August 3, 2026, identified 594 records; 33 studies were eligible. Fifteen studies reported mean absolute errors (MAEs) on the METLIN Small Molecule Retention Time (SMRT) dataset across at least seven differently filtered subsets. Among 13 models evaluated under a broad retained-only convention, the spread from best to worst was 18 s, compared to the 36 s mean repeat-measurement variability observed on SMRT reference standards. Unseen chromatographic methods were rarely tested; one model’s error rose from 29.3 s internally to 596.8 s on a held-out gradient. Random molecular partitions remained common, including in studies using cross-validation or transfer-set deduplication. Risk of bias was low in 18 studies for model development and 19 for performance evaluation, but in only seven for leakage control and one for generalizability. Reported accuracy depends as much on benchmark construction as on architecture. To support reliable compound identification, these models need structure-aware and method-aware validation with uncertainty estimates.

paper_title: Water-Damaged Buildings and Health: An Updated Review of the Evidence, Sources of Bias, and Co-Occurring Conditions
paper_abstract: Background. Water damage in buildings produces a mixture that includes fungi, bacteria, endotoxin, microbial fragments, and moisture-driven chemical emissions. The respiratory evidence has been graded; evidence on the multisystem symptoms many people report has been graded limited or inadequate, or not graded. Objectives. To summarize the evidence as of 2026; to examine how confounding, reporting bias, the composition of the exposure mixture, and co-occurring clinical conditions bear on the observed associations; and to propose a protocol for a rigorous future review. Methods. Structured evidence review (PubMed, Europe PMC, agency sources) with structured supplementary searches by body system and by exposure agent in November 2026 (145 database strategies); no registered protocol or duplicate screening. Results. The IOM and WHO graded no outcome as causal; two later reviews judged the evidence causal for asthma exacerbation in children, whereas a 2024 GRADE review rated effects in people with asthma uncertain. Pooled respiratory odds ratios are about 1.3 to 1.8, smaller in cohorts, and change modestly with socioeconomic adjustment. Measured agents such as endotoxin show both adverse and inverse associations. No epidemiological study of metabolic, hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, or cancer outcomes, or of occupants' gut microbiome, was identified; these gaps indicate neither presence nor absence of an effect. No identified study systematically screened exposed people for bile acid malabsorption, iron deficiency, thyroid disease, sleep apnea, perimenopause, celiac disease, or postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. HLA-DR typing has not been shown to provide diagnostic information. Conclusions. The respiratory and allergic evidence is sufficient to establish association. Beyond the airway, associations are reported for mental health, general symptoms, child neurodevelopment, skin, immune markers, and sarcoidosis, mostly in cross-sectional and self-reported designs; for metabolic, hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, and cancer outcomes no epidemiological study was identified. The studies that would establish or exclude these associations have not been carried out, and tests used to assess exposure and susceptibility in an individual have not been validated for that purpose. The review sets out the design that research capable of answering these questions would require.

paper_title: The Daydreaming Factory: A Twin-Calibrated Simulation Framework for Proactive Reliability Exploration of Battery-Powered Rail Vehicles—A Critical Review and Research Agenda
paper_abstract: Battery-powered and electric rail vehicles move substantial dependability risk onto battery systems, thermal management, power electronics and software for which no mature fleet failure history exists. Conventional reliability methods depend on failure modes identified beforehand and calibrated by field experience that is not yet available. This critical review examines how twin-calibrated simulation can be used to explore failure possibilities proactively. The “Daydreaming Factory” a conceptual construct proposed here, not an established term is positioned against computational ideas of model-based imagination and is organised through three analytical devices: a taxonomy of virtual environments for reliability engineering, a causal-chain test from environment to reliability outcome, and a five-level evidence-maturity scale. The enabling methods are reviewed: multi-domain co-simulation, scenario generation and rare-event search, fault injection, degradation integration, and verification, validation and uncertainty quantification. A six-component reference framework with an explicit credibility layer is specified. Assessed against the sources examined, the individual methods are mature in adjacent domains, but integrated railway-specific implementations, field validation, qualification pathways and measured reliability benefits are largely absent. A research agenda and candidate performance indicators are proposed. The review is narrative rather than systematic and the framework has not been experimentally validated.

paper_title: Same Papers, Different Verdicts: Tracing Version Drift in LLM Peer Review
paper_abstract: Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them. Stating a 30% acceptance rate in the prompt leaves a gap of 79 points between the two Opus versions. When score-stripped critiques are swapped between versions, the later critiques alone lower the accept share by 35 points for Opus and 51 for Gemini; for Opus the drop is 35 points under a third-party scorer and 24 after a rewrite that keeps each technical point and removes evaluative wording. On 57 papers, the percentiles of Opus 4.6 and 5.5 correlate at 0.73 while their accept shares differ by 44 points. On 99 to 119 submissions, the self-estimated percentiles of three models correlate with two human reviewers more strongly than a third reviewer does (point estimates 0.17 to 0.21, 95% intervals between -0.04 and +0.42). All twenty models give a 2 or a 3 in 473 of their 475 reviews, against 60 of 72 human reviews. Retrospective tests on decided papers can draw on memory. Claude Opus 5.5 names the true first author of 27 decided ICLR 2026 papers from their titles alone, with no wrong name, and Claude Opus 4.6 accepted all 11 decided papers it said it recognized, against 5 expected. Thresholds on LLM-reviewer scores therefore have to be validated against human decisions for each model version; our tests against the ICLR 2027 decisions follow on 16 December 2026.
comments: 19 pages, 5 figures. Results of the registered tests that need the ICLR 2027 decisions will be added after 16 December 2026

paper_title: Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
paper_abstract: The emergence of foundation models has marked a transformative shift in AI, enabling robust generalization across diverse downstream tasks through putative zero-shot learning. Large Language Models and Vision Language Models have demonstrated strong capabilities in tasks such as image interpretation, report generation, and question answering by effectively learning from multimodal data-images paired with associated text often with minimal supervision. In the healthcare domain, this ability to align visual and textual information reduces the reliance on extensive manual annotations, as models can leverage existing clinical reports and imaging data to learn meaningful representations. This integration holds promise for improving diagnostic support, treatment planning, and overall patient care, even in data constrained settings. In this review, we provide a definitive taxonomy of the medical VLM landscape, tracing the evolution from early Contrastive Alignment and Generative MLLMs to the cutting edge frontiers of Dense Pixel Grounding, Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), and Reasoning Incentivized (RL) architectures. We critically examine the "medical bottleneck" identifying the persistent challenges of data scarcity, the "hallucination" risks in generative diagnostics, the computational strain of 3D volumetric processing, and the lack of standardized, clinically grounded evaluation metrics.

paper_title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
paper_abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

paper_title: RTLReviewBench: LLM Hardware Reviewers Rarely Miss Bugs but Routinely Reject Correct RTL
paper_abstract: Hardware teams increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) to review register-transfer level (RTL) code, yet it is unclear whether a model can tell a correct module from a buggy one without simulating it. We introduce RTLReviewBench, a benchmark of 114 matched pairs of buggy and correct Verilog modules. Each pair shares one specification, most buggy modules are real failures of LLM code generators, and every label is confirmed by simulation. Evaluating 12 commercial and open-weight models, we find a consistent asymmetry: reviewers rarely accept buggy code but often reject correct code, producing more than five false rejections for every missed bug. Synthetic mutants hide part of the problem: on the same designs, models miss far fewer injected bugs than real ones. Asking a model to reason before it commits to a verdict sharply reduces false rejections for weaker reviewers, and a controlled ablation shows that where the reasoning appears in the output matters more than the instruction to reason, whereas sampling and majority voting do not help. A blinded audit further shows that some correct "buggy" verdicts rest on false technical claims. We release the benchmark, a harder split for future models, all model responses, and the evaluation code at https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench
comments: 24 pages, 6 figures, 16 tables. Benchmark, model responses, and code: https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench

paper_title: SurveyWeave: An Agentic Framework for Automated Survey Generation
paper_abstract: Surveys help researchers keep up with fast-moving fields, but they take weeks to months to write. Automated survey generation (AutoSurvey) can alleviate this situation, but it is challenging to draw on hundreds to thousands of precisely scoped papers, choose among many valid structures, and stay faithful to its sources while offering insights. We present SurveyWeave, an agentic architecture that decomposes the problem into four tasks coordinated by three agents, each reviewing others' work and conducting revisions based on feedback. We also introduce WeaveEval, a five-dimension evaluation grounded in prior surveys. A comprehensive comparison shows that SurveyWeave outperforms Codex by 8 points and the strongest AutoSurvey baseline by 6 points.

paper_title: Continuous-Space Diffusion and Flow Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Continuous-space diffusion and flow language models generate text by updating real-valued vectors (such as token embeddings, compressed codes, or sentence vectors) and decoding them into discrete words at readout. We organize this literature by three coupled choices: the continuous state being refined, the transition operator that updates it, and the text interface that converts states into tokens. Because language is discrete while the state space is continuous, adapting image diffusion to text encounters rounding ambiguity and embedding collapse under squared-error regression, uninformative noise schedules, distribution shift between clean-text codecs and learned priors, and mode averaging in few-step sampling. Across published comparisons with autoregressive and discrete-diffusion baselines, continuous models show no general advantage over same-scale autoregressive models on open-ended text; the closest prompt-continuation tie uses different training sequence lengths and separately tuned samplers. RePlaid matches or improves upon masked diffusion in likelihood bounds past compute-optimal budgets, and large-scale blockwise adaptation brings continuous models close to masked baselines on mathematical reasoning and code; however, continuous models still trail autoregressive baselines in held-out likelihood bounds, and scaling fits indicate that matching exact autoregressive negative log-likelihood requires substantially more training compute. Their clearest gains over autoregressive decoding appear in gradient-guided control, plan-level diversity, and task-specific reasoning after targeted fine-tuning. Under few-step budgets, trajectory-consistent distillation and stochastic bridges prevent entropy collapse, yet no standalone continuous generator has shown an end-to-end latency win over optimized autoregressive decoding at matched quality; the reported matched-quality latency gains rely on autoregressive verification of continuous drafts. We close with open problems in likelihood scaling, readout fidelity, few-step serving, representation reuse, and post-training. Project Page: https://github.com/TokenRhythm/awesome-cdllm.

paper_title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
paper_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under four years the field has grown from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. VLA research joins robotics, computer vision and language modelling, so this survey is written for researchers and practitioners from each of these fields. It reviews 89 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. Seven design axes follow a VLA's life cycle: model design (inputs and memory, architecture, action output, intermediate predictions), training (pretraining data, post-training) and deployment (real-time execution). We compare 22 models on these axes, with their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge. (i) Training data has broadened beyond teleoperated robot data (about 10,000 hours for $π_0$) to community-collected episodes and egocentric human video (20,000 hours for GR00T N1.7). (ii) Model sizes have split into two groups: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters; a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs. (iii) Generalist VLAs handling both manipulation and navigation are emerging, such as UniVLA and Qwen-VLA. We also compare VLAs with world-action models, which predict future observations as well as actions, and review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail after small scene changes. A practitioner's guide gives a default for each design decision, and a glossary supports readers new to the field.

paper_title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Forestry: A Survey of Its Development, Applications, Current Opinions and Future Directions
paper_abstract: Software has supported forest management decisions since the 1970s, from growth simulators to reinforcement learning. Since 2023, large language models (LLMs) have been combined with tools, retrieval, memory and planning to form artificial intelligence (AI) agents that analyse forest data, decide on a sequence of steps, and either advise a person or act through software and machines. This survey reviews agentic AI in forestry. It traces the development of agent concepts in the field, describes the components that current agentic systems share, and reviews applications in seven areas, from forest inventory to biodiversity monitoring. We found only 13 LLM-based agentic systems in forestry. Most are single LLM agents or small groups of role-based agents that coordinate perception models, geospatial databases and retrieval over documents. Their evaluation relies on case studies, small expert panels and public datasets, and none of the reviewed LLM-based agents controls forest machines in the field. Recurring problems are factual errors, weak spatial reasoning, missing connectivity in forests, the cybersecurity of connected machines and trust, and current evaluations are short compared with the decades over which forest decisions take effect. We derive research directions on evaluation with forest simulators, edge deployment, interoperability, graded human oversight and safety constraints for forest machines. A comparison with agriculture identifies designs that can be transferred, and we expect agents to become routine first in analysis and advice, then in planning with forest models, and only later in the supervision of forest machines.

paper_title: A Mixed-Method Assessment of Environmental Accessibility in Canadian Office Spaces: A Triangulation of IAQ Testing, Occupant Health Surveys, Scent-Free Policy Implementation, and Lived Experience
paper_abstract: With individuals spending approximately 90% of their time indoors, indoor air quality (IAQ) is a critical public health and environmental accessibility concern. Fragranced consumer products emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs), potentially creating barriers for individuals with multiple chemical sensitivity (MCS) and other health vulnerabilities. This convergent mixed-methods study integrated five evidence streams: IAQ measurements, occupant surveys, scent-free policy assessments, product emissions testing, and focus groups to examine chemical exposures and environmental accessibility in Canadian offices. Findings indicated substantial contributions from indoor VOC sources. Despite greater mechanical ventilation, non-scent-free environments exhibited higher VOC concentrations and indoor/outdoor ratios, emphasizing source control alongside ventilation. Scent-free environments generally had lower VOC concentrations, although residual exposures persisted. Overlapping VOCs detected in indoor air and consumer products, alongside policy implementation gaps, highlighted ongoing exposure prevention challenges. Occupants of scent-free workplaces reported more symptoms and chronic conditions, potentially reflecting greater reliance on these environments among vulnerable individuals. Focus-group findings further identified persistent accessibility barriers and challenges with policy implementation. Overall, findings support integrated strategies combining scent-free policies, low-emission product procurement, transparent labelling, effective source control, adequate ventilation, and consistent implementation to reduce chemical exposures and advance environmental accessibility in workplaces.

paper_title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Judicial Processes: A Socio-Technical Scoping Review of Architectures, Tasks, and Institutional Risks (2023–Mid-2026)
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in legal research, litigation support, and judicial administration. This scoping review maps architectures, court-facing tasks, evaluation designs, and institutional risks in research on GenAI and large language models (LLMs). Framed by Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported with PRISMA-ScR, it screened 1,518 Scopus and Web of Science records (31 March 2026) and 1,000 supplementary Elicit results (July 2026) for publications from 2023 onward, which yielded 201 references. We then reassessed each reference against explicit GenAI and judicial relevance criteria in an AI-assisted workflow checked by one author, with a second screening by a different LLM, and recorded the decisions and reasons. We charted publication characteristics and primary evidence designs and checked selected outcomes against the original publications. The synthesis includes 189 publications. We retained 10 references for context and excluded 2. Offline model evaluations accounted for 106 publications (56.1%). Studies reported task-specific results for retrieval, summarization, prediction, and drafting. One audit of three commercial legal research tools found hallucinations in 17–33% of evaluated queries. The mapped evidence is consistent with source-grounded, reviewable assistance for defined tasks. Heterogeneous evaluations and limited evidence from operating courts constrain conclusions about routine judicial use.

paper_title: K-Pop Fandom and Parasocial Relationships Across Cultural Contexts: A Text-Mining Review of Emotional Attachment and Social Identity from a Cultural Psychology Perspective
paper_abstract: Research on K-pop fandom has grown rapidly, yet its literature on parasocial relationships, emotional attachment and social identity is dispersed across psychology, communication, marketing and tourism studies, which makes it hard to see what has been studied and how it is framed. This review applies text mining to a purposive corpus of 245 scholarly records on K-pop fandom and parasocial relationships, drawn from the reference list of this manuscript and not from a systematic database search. The scope is research on K-pop fans in any country; the review asks how the literature is framed, how often South Korea is named as a setting, and which topics key studies address on platforms, fan communities and local cultural contexts. Record titles and venues were analysed with term and n-gram frequencies, a ten-theme dictionary compared across three publication periods, non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) topic modelling and a term co-occurrence network. These results describe how records are titled and grouped; they are not findings about fans. In this corpus, 70% of dated records appeared in 2024–2026 and journal articles make up 66%. Consumption and marketing (n = 75) and parasocial interaction (n = 59) are the most prevalent themes. Six topics and four network communities emerged (modularity = 0.34); terms for attachment and purchase intention co-occur in titles, but the relationship between these constructs can only be assessed from the studies themselves. South Korea is named in only a few titles or venues, whereas Indonesia is named most often, although study settings were not verified from abstracts or full texts. A narrative overview of key studies identifies research on platform-mediated intimacy, on fan communities as sites of both belonging and strain, and on local cultural contexts; individual study findings and settings were not verified against abstracts or full texts. We outline a research agenda for comparative, culturally grounded studies, including verified studies of Korean domestic fans.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Planning and Routing Strategies for UAV-Based Search and Rescue Operations: Methods, Evidence, and Research Gaps
paper_abstract: This paper reports a systematic literature review of planning and routing strategies for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in search and rescue (SAR). The review followed a documented protocol and is reported according to PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. From 3,642 database records and 96 titles from exploratory searches and the research group's collection, 54 studies were assessed in full text, and 46 primary studies published from 2021 to 2026 were included. Each study was classified by its presence model, detection model, and objective, and by route structure, revisiting, energy, coordination, risk, and validation. Quality, risk of bias, and level of evidence were also assessed. Coverage routing is the largest strategy family (16 studies), and metaheuristics are the most common method class (13). Risk of bias is high in 26 studies, 23 studies are purely synthetic, and only three flew real aircraft. Eight studies build a cell-wise presence map but treat detection as certain, only two calibrate detection against empirical data, and no study places ground risk in the cost of travel. Seventeen studies report an optimality reference, but only six extend it to the application scale. A pooled effect cannot be computed, so 52 observations from 31 studies are synthesized by stratum. Of twelve tracked gaps, seven were narrowed, four were confirmed, and one was maintained. The main gap is the combination of modeling elements. The median study meets three of nine tracked requirements, and the closest study meets eight but keeps closed routes and unbounded revisiting. No multi-vehicle routing formulation has had its predicted detection probability compared with field measurements. This extended version reports the complete protocol and the per-study classifications.

paper_title: Forty Years of The Legend of Zelda: A Scoping Review of Game Design, Computation, Culture, and Play
paper_abstract: Over four decades, The Legend of Zelda has evolved from a landmark action-adventure series into a recurring object of research across game studies, computer science, musicology, cultural studies, psychology, education, and related fields. This article presents a scoping review and structured survey of Zelda-related research across the franchise’s 1986–2026 history, examining how the series has been studied as a designed system, cultural artifact, interactive narrative, audiovisual environment, player-community object, and computational testbed. Following a PRISMA-ScR-informed process with duplicate screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 93 studies were included in the final synthesis: 52 Core scholarly studies, 40 complementary scholarly/grey-literature studies, and one complementary critical/industry record. The literature is strongly recent and unevenly distributed: 65 included studies were published from 2020 onward, while 44 explicitly address either Ocarina of Time or Breath of the Wild.
